title: introduce-flashstream-multipass-attn-and-rotary-delta-fusion
author: Aisha Gupta
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token cost and P95 latency for long-context text generation workloads by avoiding redundant rotary/rope recomputation and minimizing intermediate copies during attention. This PR introduces a new multipass attention kernel (FlashStream) that streams attention tiles through compute in a constant working set, plus a rotary-delta fusion that applies incremental rotary transforms to cached KV shards instead of full re-rotation on every request. The combined changes target model-serving scenarios with long prefix caching and continuous batching where memory pressure and copy overhead dominate. Key design points: 1) FlashStream multipass kernel: tile-based streaming that computes QK and accumulates softmaxed values in-place to reduce peak activation memory. It supports variable tile sizes chosen at runtime based on sequence length distribution and chosen kernel heuristics. 2) Rotary-delta fusion: KV cache now stores a compact delta rotation state per shard; on appends we apply a small, fused rotation update to the relevant KV rows avoiding a full pass. This reduces per-request rotary ops when using large cached prefixes. 3) Mixed-precision accumulation safeguards with an optional FP32 accumulation path for high variance batches (configurable via runtime flag). 4) Scheduler hooks: new continuous-batching hint that pins short latency-critical requests to the fastpath and routes long streaming requests through the multipass kernel, improving tail latency. 5) Compatibility: a fallback to the legacy FlashAttn kernel remains for short sequences and some model variants. Benchmarks (internal): - A100, 32k context, 8-token streaming increments: overall throughput +15% to +18% and P95 latency -20% compared to current main; cost/unit token reduced ~12% with conservative batching. - V100 tests show smaller wins (~6-9%) but lower memory footprint. Changes and tests: unit tests for rotary correctness added, end-to-end generation harness updated, new microbench for multipass kernel, and scheduler simulation added. Migration: opt-in runtime flag (flashstream.enabled) defaulting to off for initial rollout. Checklist: - [x] kernel implementation and CUDA unit tests - [x] runtime integration and scheduler hooks - [x] Python bindings and examples updated - [x] perf harness and baseline numbers - [x] documentation update (draft) - [x] smoke tests across a few model families

ci_summary: Initial CI run: build fail on doc lint + one perf harness flaky test. After fixing doc header and deterministic seed the rerun passed all checks (unit, integration, perf smoke). Benchmarks recorded as artifacts.
release_notes: Introduce FlashStream multipass attention kernel and rotary-delta fusion. Opt-in via flashstream.enabled. Expected improvements for long-context workloads: ~15% throughput and ~20% P95 latency improvement on A100; config flags allow toggling FP32 accumulation for numerical stability. Rollout gradual with runtime flag and metrics monitoring.
notes: Backported minimal format compatibility code so existing KV serializers can still read legacy snapshots. Performance artifacts stored under CI build 2026-02-24-45103. Runtime flag used to gate rollout to avoid immediate production exposure.
